test_intent: Verify that calling Approve then RemoveApproval on a mocked IUserManager returns expected values and methods are called once.
reason: Test exercises a mock against itself: sets up _userManagerMock to return predetermined values, then asserts those same values. No production UserManager implementation is exercised. The mock returns what it was told to return, so no real behavior is protected. No distinct bot contract exists beyond the general happy path of calling interface methods.

test_intent: Verify that after calling Approve on a mocked IUserManager, Approved returns true and both methods were called once.
reason: Pure mock choreography: mock is set up to return true for Approved, then test asserts Approved returns true. No real UserManager logic is exercised. The test cannot catch any regression because it only validates that the mock returns its configured value. No distinct bot contract beyond calling interface methods.

test_intent: Verify that calling Approve twice on the same user via a mock IUserManager results in exactly two calls.
reason: Mock choreography: calls Approve twice on a mock, verifies Times.Exactly(2). The mock cannot simulate real idempotency or state management behavior. No production UserManager logic is exercised. Testing that a mock was called twice when you explicitly called it twice is tautological.

test_intent: Verify that calling Approve and InBanlist concurrently (10 tasks) on a mock IUserManager results in correct call counts.
reason: Mock choreography with fake concurrency: creates 10 tasks calling mock methods, verifies call counts. A mock cannot exercise real thread-safety or concurrency concerns in UserManager. The test only proves Task.WhenAll completes and the mock was called the expected number of times. No real concurrency behavior is tested.

test_intent: Verify that concurrent Approve and Approved calls across 5 different user IDs on a mock IUserManager result in correct call counts per user.
reason: Mock choreography with fake concurrency across multiple users: sets up mock for 5 user IDs, creates 10 tasks, verifies per-user call counts. test_intent: Verify that a very large user ID (999999999999) works correctly with Approved and InBanlist on a mock IUserManager.
reason: Mock choreography with an edge-case input: uses a large user ID with mock methods that return predetermined values. The mock does not exercise any real UserManager logic that could fail on large IDs. No production behavior is protected; the test only verifies the mock returns its configured false values. If real UserManager had an issue with large IDs, this test would not catch it.
